findings.what: fix commits 2c0b4e7 and 4012f0e carry no Fixes-Finding trailer, so no trailer links the A1 fixes to I1-I8
findings.why: The requirements-trace skill says every fix(...) commit carries Fixes-Finding. The commit-msg hook accepts the round form A1/I1 (lines 27-29), so G9 did not block this. 2c0b4e7 should name A1/I1 to A1/I8. 4012f0e fixes a gate observation, not a finding, so its fix( prefix has no finding to cite. Because the trailer is missing, the trail links a fix to its finding only through the commit body text.

findings.rule_id: F5-acceptance: AzureCLI@2 deploy; managed identity to Entra-only SQL
findings.what: The SQL steps set azureSubscription: $(sqlServiceConnection) from a job-level variable group; service connections must resolve when the pipeline compiles, so this may fail resource authorization
findings.why: Azure DevOps authorizes service connections before the run, and a macro variable that resolves at runtime is a known cause of 'service connection could not be found'. I can't confirm from here whether a job-level variable group resolves in time, and it was never run (az and DevOps were never used). The ARM connection already uses a compile-time template parameter (azureServiceConnection). A second template parameter would remove the risk, and the checker's I8 assertion would still pass. Please have the investigator verify this before David has to defend it.

findings.what: The I5 pool check only requires that 'vmImage' is absent, so a deployment job with its pool deleted (the default Microsoft-hosted pool) still passes
findings.why: The assertion is meant to prove that the SQL steps run inside the network. All it rejects is an explicit vmImage key. Asserting that pool.name is present (for example, the policies-<env>-vnet pattern) would stop a mutant without a pool from passing. The infrastructure at HEAD is correct (pool.name is set). The gap is the oracle's strength.

findings.rule_id: F5-acceptance: no secrets / least privilege (I8 trade-off text)
findings.what: The comment says 'a leaked pipeline token cannot administer the server', but the ARM service connection in the same job can rewrite the server's Entra admin through ARM
findings.why: A subscription-scope deployment needs Contributor-level rights, and with them it can write Microsoft.Sql/servers administrators. The split does keep the SQL connection to database scope, which is a real gain. But the sentence as written claims more than that, and an Azure reviewer will challenge it. Scope the claim to the SQL service connection's token, or name the ARM path as an accepted residual risk. Code-quality rule: comments must be explainable and true.

First-run ordering, for David: the bootstrap happens after the first infrastructure deployment, so on an environment's first run the Apply migrations step fails until an admin runs the bootstrap. The template implies this but does not say it.
The database user is named after the app (app-policies-<env>), while the identity is id-policies-<env>. With WITH SID, TYPE = E, the name is only a label, but David may be asked why the two differ.
